newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Slovak steel signs JV with Czech.
newsitem.headline: Slovak steel signs JV with Czech.

text.p: Slovak steel maker Zeleziarne Podbrezova a.s. said on Monday it had signed a joint venture contract with Czech steelworks Vitkovice a.s. to help revitalise its steel forging mill from early 1997.

"We signed the contract establishing a 50-50 joint-venture with Vitkovice to produce forged steel pipes at one of its already operating mills," Marian Kurcik, Finance Director at Podbrezova, told Reuters.
"The venture should be a step towards revitalising the mill's operation and also us, as we will sell the venture most of its inputs -- rolled steel pipes," Kurcik said.
Vitkovice officials were not immediately available.

Under the contract, Podbrezova will pay Vitkovice 25 million Czech crowns to add towards the venture's basic capital by the end of the year. The Slovak Finance Ministry is expected to approve the payment soon, Kurcik added.
Vitkovice's share would be equal to Podbrezova's, but provided through capital such as buildings, equipment and supplies, he said.

Kurcik said there was "no correlation" between this contract and the expected privatisation of a 16-18 percent stake in Vitkovice, declining to say whether Podbrezova was or was not interested in the stake.
Zeleziarne Popdbrezova is Slovakia's main steel pipe producer. It exported two-thirds of its last year's production to western Europe.
"Our current rolled-steel production of 120,000 tonnes a year, at 70-75 percent of current capacity and should rise by some 10,000 tonnes a year due to the join-venture," Kurcik said.
Podbrezova also produces some 30,000 tonnes of forged rolled-steel pipes a year, but Kurcik said this production line is already at full capacity.
